extraction.name: SWE-rebench
extraction.description: A public dataset of over 21,000 interactive Python-based software engineering tasks collected automatically from real-world GitHub repositories, suitable for training and benchmarking software engineering agents.
extraction.creator: Ibragim Badertdinov, Alexander Golubev, Maksim Nekrashevich, Anton Shevtsov, Simon Karasik, Andrei Andriushchenko, Maria Trofimova, Daria Litvintseva, Boris Yangel
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was built with a fully automated four-stage pipeline: preliminary task collection from GitHub Archive and GitHub, automated installation instruction configuration, execution-based installation verification, and automated instance quality assessment.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web API, Software Collection, Document analysis
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data came from GitHub Archive daily JSON event archives and cloned GitHub repositories with full commit histories, including issue descriptions, discussions, linked pull requests, metadata, merge status, commits, and repository files.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Issues were linked with pull requests, filtered by repository language, license, resolution status, merge status, issue length, test modifications, and file-change count. For each selected pull request, the patch was split into a solution patch for non-test files and a test patch for test files. Tasks were also grouped by normalized project versions inferred from git tags.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The pipeline performed preliminary filtering, automated environment setup generation with LLMs, iterative recipe refinement using error logs, execution-based verification in containers, test-log parsing, final container building, dependency freezing, and automated quality scoring.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Task instances were annotated automatically with LLM-generated quality labels for Issue Clarity, Task Complexity, and Test Patch Correctness by fine-tuning Qwen 2.5-72B-Instruct on human annotations from SWE-bench Verified and predicting each binary label independently.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The paper reports validation performance of the fine-tuned annotation model on a 75/25 train/validation split with 413 validation examples, including accuracy and weighted F1 for each label, and notes that the automated assessment is imperfect but useful for filtering.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset and benchmark are intended to be continuously updated with fresh tasks, with ongoing evaluation of existing and additional models and sharing analyses with the community.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark may accelerate development of increasingly autonomous AI systems in software engineering, with risks such as overreliance on AI-generated code or misuse of automated agents for introducing vulnerabilities; the authors argue that openness, decontaminated evaluations, and rigorous benchmarking help mitigate these concerns.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset is restricted to Python repositories with permissive licenses, and the automated pipeline relies on heuristics and LLM-driven interpretations that can introduce errors.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The fully automated pipeline can produce imperfectly described or unsolvable tasks, lowering absolute success rates compared to manually curated benchmarks. The initial release is limited exclusively to Python, and the LLM-based installation and quality assessment methods were validated on limited data and cannot fully replicate nuanced human judgment.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for training and benchmarking software engineering agents, particularly reinforcement learning-based approaches, and for building contamination-free evaluation benchmarks.

name.evidence: Using this pipeline, we construct SWE-rebench, a public dataset comprising over 21,000 interactive Python-based SWE tasks

description.evidence: Using this pipeline, we construct SWE-rebench, a public dataset comprising over 21,000 interactive Python-based SWE tasks, suitable for reinforcement leaming of SWE agents at scale.

creator.evidence: Ibragim Badertdinov ... Alexander Golubev ... Maksim Nekrashevich ... Anton Shevtsov ... Simon Karasik ... Andrei Andriushchenko ... Maria Trofimova ... Daria Litvintseva ... Boris Yangel

inLanguage.evidence: The problem statement must be in English.

isLiveDataset.evidence: we introduce a novel, automated, and scalable pipeline to continuously extract real-world interactive SWE tasks from diverse GitHub repositories.

rai:dataCollection.evidence: Our pipeline comprises four stages: preliminary task collection, automated installation instruction configuration, execution-based installation verification, and quality assessment

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: The primary sources for our data are GitHub Archive [Grigorik, 2011] and GitHub. ... Each day, it publishes a JSON archive listing all GitHub events from that day. ... We clone relevant GitHub repositories with their full commit histories to our local storage. ... An LLM scans repository files (e.g., README.md, Dockerfile, setup.py) to find potential sources of installation information.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: The primary sources for our data are GitHub Archive [Grigorik, 2011] and GitHub. ... We use this archive to collect detailed data about issues: issue description, discussion, linked pull requests, and metadata such as creation date and labels. We also extract information about pull requests, including their merge status, last commit, and discussions. ... We clone relevant GitHub repositories with their full commit histories to our local storage.

rai:dataCollectionTimeframe.evidence: To initiate the dataset building process, we download approximately 450,000 pull requests linked to issues created before May 1, 2025.

rai:dataManipulationProtocol.evidence: We then link issues with pull requests that mention resolving them in their title or description, applying filters to select instances where: ... The PR must introduces or modifies tests and includes code changes beyond test files. ... Changes affect 1 to 15 files. ... For each selected pull request, the overall patch is divided into two components: a solution patch, containing changes to non-test files intended to address the issue, and a test patch, comprising only changes to test files. ... We group these task instances by project versions inferred from git tag outputs, normalizing versions to major.minor format

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: This filtering aims to eliminate unsuitable candidates, particularly those lacking tests. ... We use the Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct model ... to generate up to three candidate JSON recipes per task. If an error occurs during the subsequent scripted installation or test execution ... the LLM attempts to refine that recipe by analyzing error logs and the original instructions ... To confirm task solvability and the integrity of the provided tests, we perform execution-based installation verification. ... Record exact dependency versions (via pip freeze, conda env export) after a successful setup ... To assess these properties automatically, we fine-tune an instruction-following model using human annotations from SWE-bench Verified

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: To assess these properties automatically, we fine-tune an instruction-following model using human annotations from SWE-bench Verified to predict: • Issue Clarity ... • Task Complexity ... • Test Patch Correctness ... We fine-tune Qwen 2.5-72B-Instruct using annotations from SWE-bench Verified. ... It is then prompted to predict one of three binary quality labels ... We train the model to predict each label independently

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: We train the model to predict each label independently; each task instance is assessed for each quality characteristic separately using a 75/25 training/validation split (total 413 validation examples). ... For Task Complexity ... our fine-tuned model achieved 81% accuracy and a weighted F1-score of 0.82. ... For Test Patch Correctness ... the model achieved 67% accuracy ... For Issue Clarity ... it achieved 79% accuracy ... While this automated assessment is not perfect, these labels offer users a means to filter the dataset

rai:annotationsPerItem.evidence: The LLM-generated labels for Issue Clarity, Task Complexity, and Test Patch Correctness are provided as metadata with each task instance.

rai:machineAnnotationTools.evidence: We use the Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct model [Qwen et al., 2025] ... to generate up to three candidate JSON recipes per task. ... We fine-tune Qwen 2.5-72B-Instruct using annotations from SWE-bench Verified.

rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan.evidence: A public SWE-rebench leaderboard that offers continuously updated, decontaminated, and standardized evaluations ... • Keeping SWE-rebench benchmark up-to-date: Maintaining evaluation process on fresh tasks for the existing models, evaluating a wider range of LLMs and sharing detailed performance analyses with the community.

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: Finally, while our benchmark is intended to support transparency and standardization in evaluating SWE agents, it may also accelerate the development of increasingly autonomous AI systems in software engineering. This progress brings potential risks, such as overreliance on AI-generated code or misuse of automated agents for introducing vulnerabilities. We believe that fostering openness, decontaminated evaluations, and rigorous benchmarking practices helps mitigate these concems

rai:dataBiases.evidence: To initiate the dataset building process, we download approximately 450,000 pull requests linked to issues created before May 1, 2025. These originate from over 30,000 repositories that feature permissive licenses ... and where Python constitutes over 75% of the codebase lines of code. ... While our multi-stage filtering, refinements to existing methodologies and automated dependency installation are designed for robustness at scale, they rely on heuristics and LLM-driven interpretations.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: We outline following main limitations of our work: • Automated task quality assessment: While we employ automated quality assessment, the fully automated pipeline may result in some tasks being imperfectly described or unsolvable solely from the issue. This can lead to lower absolute success rates compared to manually curated benchmarks. • Limited language diversity: The initial release of SWE-rebench is limited exclusively to Python ... Similarly, the automated task quality assessment ... serves as a valuable scalable proxy but cannot fully replicate nuanced human judgment

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: SWE-rebench, a public dataset of more than 21,000 interactive Python-based SWE tasks, designed to train and benchmark agents in diverse executable environments, particularly suitable for reinforcement leaming-based approaches. ... Additionally, we use continuous supply of fresh tasks collected using SWE-rebench methodology to build a contamination-free benchmark for agentic software engineering.
